html: Pneumonia means germs have taken hold deep in the lungs. The tiny air pockets there swell and can fill with fluid, so less oxygen gets through. Some people recover at home with treatment; others need a hospital stay.

• A cough that brings up yellow, green or rust-colored phlegm
  • Fever, sweats or shaking
  • Getting winded with little effort
  • Sharp chest pain when you take a deep breath
  • In older adults, sudden confusion may be the main sign

• Stay current on the vaccines your care team recommends, including flu shots
  • Wash your hands often
  • Don't smoke
Breathing feels hard, your fever won't break, or you're getting worse instead of better after a few days. Babies, adults over 65 and people with weakened immune systems should be seen sooner.

title: Pneumonia
abstract: How a lung infection makes breathing harder, and when to be seen.
